goal: Redesign `senti flow resume` as a recovery-only entry point that discovers ambiguous flow candidates, selects only explicitly recoverable targets, and hands a verified `runId` target to later continuation commands without contaminating normal `/senti.flow` active-flow resolution.

in: Clarify and implement responsibilities for `senti flow resume`, `senti flow get resolve-context`, normal active-flow resolution, and target-aware continuation.
Keep broad `scanAllFlows()` discovery limited to explicit recovery/discovery behavior, not normal active-flow detection.
Make candidates shown by recovery discovery selectable with `senti flow resume --spec <specId>` only when they carry a usable `runId`.
Require `runId` for normal continuation after resume recovery; candidates without `runId` are displayed for diagnosis and blocked from continuation.
Update `senti.flow-resume` so it gives guarded continuation or safe-stop instructions instead of unqualified `/senti.flow` re-entry.
Define recovery candidate states for stale, finalized, orphan worktree, and branch-only flows.
out: Unrelated changes to the normal new-flow `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` application boundary.
Prior normal flow entry-side fixes unless directly required by the recovery contract.

constraints: Use only Node.js built-in modules; do not add external dependencies.
Do not put project-specific values in `src/` package code.
After editing `src/skills/**`, run `senti upgrade` so generated skill files are updated.
Migration parity applies: retained public command behavior must be inventoried, mapped to the new owner, and verified with behavior-level tests.
Normal active-flow resolution must not call broad branch/worktree discovery.
Recovery discovery must preserve bounded scanning: at most `SCAN_FLOWS_LIMIT` candidates, currently 200, across local specs, git worktrees, and `feature/*` branches.
design_principles: Recovery discovery and normal active-flow execution are separate paths.
`runId` is the only safe identity for normal continuation after resume recovery.
Displayed recovery candidates that cannot be safely continued should explain their state instead of disappearing silently.
Target guards must fail before any continuation step can act on a different flow.

modules.text: `src/lib/flow-manager.js` owns active-flow registry resolution and broad flow scanning.
`src/flow/lib/run-resume.js` owns the recovery/discovery command surface and selected target envelope.
`src/flow/lib/resolve-context-envelope.js` owns the normal active-flow context envelope shared with `get resolve-context`.
`src/lib/flow-target-guard.js` owns target mismatch checks used by guarded status, next-action, and run continuation.
`src/skills/senti.flow-resume/SKILL.md` owns user-facing recovery guidance after context loss.

data_flow.text: Normal `/senti.flow` continuation reads registered active flow state, applies target guards when supplied, and does not inspect branch/worktree discovery candidates.
`senti flow resume` performs explicit recovery discovery, classifies active and recovery candidates, and returns candidate state without mutating normal active-flow registration.
`senti flow resume --spec <specId>` selects a discovered candidate only when it has both `runId` and an execution root. Continuation runs from that root with `--expect-run-id`.

Candidates without `runId`, without an execution root, finalized flows, stale references, and branch-only flows are displayed with state and safe-stop guidance rather than entering normal continuation.

Recovery selectability: active and orphan-worktree candidates are continuable only when `runId` and execution root exist; stale, finalized, branch-only, and missing-runId candidates are blocked/display-only.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Normal `resolveActiveFlow()` intentionally avoids `scanAllFlows()`; recovery discovery remains separate from active-flow execution.
decisions.evidence: `src/lib/flow-manager.js` documents that `resolveActiveFlow()` does not call `scanAllFlows()` because branch/worktree discovery is a recovery concern.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Current `resume --spec` only selects registered active flows, which contradicts the recovery candidate UX described in the Issue.
decisions.evidence: `src/lib/flow-manager.js` selects `opts.selectSpecId` from `.senti/.active-flow` entries and throws when the spec is not registered active.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Current `senti.flow-resume` skill instructs mainline users to invoke `/senti.flow`, losing the selected resume target.
decisions.evidence: `src/skills/senti.flow-resume/SKILL.md` says mainline phases should run `/senti.flow` after resume.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Target guard options already exist for status and next-action surfaces and should be reused for resume continuation.
decisions.evidence: `src/flow/registry.js` defines `--expect-issue`, `--expect-spec`, and `--expect-run-id` for status and next-action help.

decisions.text: `resume --spec <specId>` remains the explicit recovery selection surface rather than introducing a second selector.
decisions.evidence: Draft q1 user answer selected `resume --spec` for discovery candidate selection.
decisions.consideredAlternatives: A separate discovery-specific selection command was considered and rejected by user decision.

decisions.text: `runId` is required for normal continuation after resume recovery; `spec` and `worktreePath` are diagnostic only when `runId` is missing.
decisions.evidence: Draft q2 user answer rejected `spec + worktreePath` fallback as unsafe for continuation.

decisions.text: Continuation handoff uses the selected candidate execution root plus `--expect-run-id`; this avoids registering recovery candidates as normal active flows.
decisions.evidence: Spec review found that runId guards cannot load arbitrary candidates by themselves. The repaired contract uses cwd/root resolution plus target guard.

decisions.text: Migration inventory: `resume` discovery keeps discovery output; `resume --spec` changes selector scope; status/next-action/run keep guarded execution; resolve-context and `.active-flow` keep normal ownership.
decisions.evidence: Draft gate and spec gate required inventory for affected user-facing commands, APIs, generated state, and side effects.

decisions.text: Migration mapping: recovery discovery is owned by `senti flow resume`; normal active state remains owned by `.senti/.active-flow`; target mismatch remains owned by flow target guards.
decisions.evidence: Retained surfaces are mapped to owners rather than being merged into one resolver.

decisions.text: Behavior verification maps one public surface per check: resume discovery, resume selection, status, next-action, run, resolve-context, active registry, and resume skill guidance.
decisions.evidence: Gate migration-parity finding required behavior-level verification for each retained surface.

decisions.text: Finalized flows remain visible in discovery but are blocked from normal continuation.
decisions.evidence: Draft q3 user answer selected display-only behavior for finalized flows.

decisions.text: The resume skill must show guarded continuation or safe-stop instructions rather than only telling users to run `/senti.flow`.
decisions.evidence: Draft q4 user answer selected `runId` guard guidance.

background: `flow resume` was intended to recover context after compaction or when invoked outside the worktree, but it currently mixes candidate discovery, target selection, and continuation guidance. Broad discovery can show stale branch/worktree candidates, while `resume --spec` can only select `.senti/.active-flow` registrations. The skill then tells users to invoke `/senti.flow` without preserving the selected target, allowing a later command to continue a different flow.

requirements.desc: Normal active-flow resolution must remain registry-based and must not use broad `scanAllFlows()` recovery discovery when starting or continuing `/senti.flow`.
`senti flow resume` must act as explicit recovery discovery and classify active, stale, finalized, orphan worktree, and branch-only candidates separately from normal active flows.

`senti flow resume --spec <specId>` must select a displayed recovery candidate only when that candidate has a usable `runId` and execution root; candidates without both values must be display-only and blocked from normal continuation.

Continuation after resume recovery must run from the selected candidate execution root and verify the selected `runId` before status, next-action, or run command execution can proceed; a mismatched target must return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before step execution.

`senti.flow-resume` must stop presenting unqualified `/senti.flow` re-entry and must instead show execution-root plus `runId` guarded continuation commands when both values exist, or safe-stop instructions when either value is missing.

Migration parity must be verified for retained public surfaces: resume discovery, resume selection, normal active-flow status, target-aware status, next-action, run continuation, resolve-context, active-flow registry, and skill guidance.
At least one e2e worktree recovery case must verify real git-worktree discovery and separation from normal active-flow resolution.
Recovery discovery must keep bounded resource usage by preserving the `SCAN_FLOWS_LIMIT` candidate cap and limiting traversal to local specs, registered git worktrees, and `feature/*` branches.

acceptance_criteria: Given `.senti/.active-flow` is absent, normal `/senti.flow` new-flow startup and normal status resolution are not affected by stale candidates found by recovery discovery.

Given recovery discovery lists multiple candidates, `senti flow resume --spec <specId>` can select a displayed active or orphan-worktree candidate that has `runId` and execution root, and returns an envelope containing the selected `runId`, `spec`, and root/path context.
Given a discovery candidate lacks `runId` or execution root, `senti flow resume --spec <specId>` does not enter normal continuation and reports the candidate as display-only or blocked.
Given a finalized flow is discovered, it is labeled as finalized and blocked from normal continuation while remaining visible for diagnosis.
Given a stale reference or branch-only candidate is discovered, it is labeled as a blocked/display-only recovery candidate rather than a normal active flow.
Given an orphan worktree candidate with `runId` and execution root is discovered, it can be selected and continued from that root with `--expect-run-id`.
Given a selected `runId` and execution root, target-aware status, next-action, and run command paths run from that root, verify `runId` before acting, and return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` on mismatch.
`senti flow get resolve-context` continues to describe the normal active flow and does not include unrelated broad discovery candidates.
`senti.flow-resume` output no longer instructs users to run `/senti.flow` without target guard context.
Spec-local tests under `specs/313-resume-recovery-only/tests/` include `// spec: R<N>` headers covering the new behavior.
Behavior-level verification for `senti flow resume`: discovery lists classified recovery candidates and remains capped at `SCAN_FLOWS_LIMIT` candidates.
Behavior-level verification for `senti flow resume --spec`: selectable candidates with `runId` and execution root return a selected target envelope.
Behavior-level verification for `senti flow get status`: normal status ignores stale recovery discovery candidates, while target-aware status rejects mismatched `runId`.
Behavior-level verification for `senti flow get next-action`: guarded next-action rejects mismatched `runId` before dispatcher work.
Behavior-level verification for representative `senti flow run ...`: guarded run continuation rejects mismatched `runId` before step execution.
Behavior-level verification for `senti flow get resolve-context`: output remains the normal active-flow context envelope and does not include unrelated recovery candidates.
Behavior-level verification for `.senti/.active-flow`: recovery discovery does not register display-only candidates as normal active flows.
Behavior-level verification for `senti.flow-resume`: guidance includes execution-root plus `runId` guard instructions or safe-stop instructions.
Shared unit/e2e tests cover migration parity for CLI command behavior and skill guidance, including an e2e worktree recovery case.

clarifications.q: Can `spec + worktreePath` substitute for `runId` during continuation?
clarifications.a: No. `spec + worktreePath` may identify a displayed recovery candidate for diagnosis, but normal continuation after resume recovery requires `runId`.

clarifications.q: Can `runId` alone load an arbitrary recovery candidate?
clarifications.a: No. Normal continuation after resume recovery requires both `runId` and an execution root. Commands run from the execution root and use `--expect-run-id` to verify the selected flow.

Active and orphan-worktree candidates are continuable only when they have both `runId` and execution root. Stale references, finalized flows, branch-only candidates, and missing-runId candidates are display-only/blocked.

clarifications.q: What public behavior is migrated or retained?
clarifications.a: `senti flow resume` keeps discovery but becomes recovery-only; `resume --spec` changes from active-only selection to recovery selection with runId/root gating; status, next-action, run, resolve-context, and `.senti/.active-flow` retain normal active-flow ownership; `senti.flow-resume` changes guidance only.

clarifications.q: What resource bounds apply to recovery discovery?
clarifications.a: Discovery must preserve the existing `SCAN_FLOWS_LIMIT` cap of 200 candidates and scan only local specs, registered git worktrees, and `feature/*` branches.

clarifications.q: Should finalized flows be hidden from recovery discovery?
clarifications.a: No. They should be visible with finalized state and blocked continuation.

clarifications.q: Does this spec change npm release behavior?
clarifications.a: No. npm publish and release work are out of scope.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a separate recovery selection command instead of changing `resume --spec`.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because the user chose to make the existing `resume --spec <specId>` surface match the displayed recovery candidates.

alternatives_considered.option: Allow `spec + worktreePath` fallback for continuation when `runId` is missing.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because missing `runId` means normal continuation cannot prove it is acting on the selected flow instance.
Rejected because hiding them removes diagnostic context and makes stale/finalized candidate differences less visible.

tasks.title: Classify recovery candidates
tasks.goal: Make explicit recovery discovery classify broad scan results without changing normal active-flow resolution.
acceptance: `scanAllFlows()` output is consumed only by recovery discovery.
Recovery discovery preserves the `SCAN_FLOWS_LIMIT` candidate cap and reports truncation behavior.
Active, stale, finalized, orphan worktree, and branch-only candidates have distinguishable state in resume output.
tasks.implementation_notes: Focus on candidate modeling and discovery boundaries in flow-manager and resume code. Preserve normal resolve-context semantics.
tasks.test_strategy: Unit tests for discovery classification, candidate cap behavior, and a regression that normal active resolution ignores stale scan candidates.

tasks.title: Select resume target
tasks.goal: Make `senti flow resume --spec <specId>` select displayed candidates only when a safe `runId` exists.
acceptance: `resume --spec` selects a displayed candidate with `runId` and execution root even when `.senti/.active-flow` is absent.
A candidate without `runId` or execution root is reported as blocked/display-only and does not enter normal continuation.
Finalized, stale, and branch-only candidates are visible and blocked.
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep `spec + worktreePath` as diagnostic identity only. Do not register display-only candidates as normal active flows. Select only active or orphan-worktree candidates with `runId` and execution root.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local tests for selectable and blocked candidates; shared unit tests for `.active-flow` absent behavior.

tasks.title: Guard continuation commands
tasks.goal: Ensure continuation after resume recovery verifies selected `runId` before status, next-action, or run command execution proceeds.
acceptance: Status and next-action reject mismatched `runId` with `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before dispatcher actions.
Run command paths used after resume recovery are invoked from the selected execution root and reject mismatched `runId` before step execution.
Resolve-context remains a normal active-flow envelope and does not mix in recovery discovery candidates.
tasks.implementation_notes: Reuse existing target guard semantics where possible. The handoff contract is execution-root plus `--expect-run-id`, not global runId lookup. Extend guard parsing only where command surfaces lack it.
tasks.test_strategy: Unit tests for target mismatch on status, next-action, and representative run command paths.

tasks.title: Update resume guidance
tasks.goal: Update `senti.flow-resume` instructions to show guarded continuation or safe-stop recovery guidance.
acceptance: The skill no longer tells users to run `/senti.flow` without a target guard.
The skill names the execution root and guarded status/continuation commands when `runId` exists.
The skill tells users to stop or perform manual recovery when `runId` or execution root is absent.
tasks.implementation_notes: Update source skill files and run `senti upgrade` so generated skill artifacts are synchronized. Guidance should tell the operator to run follow-up commands from the selected execution root.
tasks.test_strategy: Skill text regression tests assert old unqualified guidance is absent and guarded guidance is present.

tasks.title: Verify recovery behavior
tasks.goal: Add spec-local and shared regression coverage for migration parity and worktree recovery.
acceptance: Spec-local tests under `specs/313-resume-recovery-only/tests/` include `// spec: R<N>` headers.
A shared e2e test covers worktree recovery discovery with real git worktree state.

Regression tests cover normal active-flow isolation, resume selection, blocked candidates, execution-root handoff, target mismatch, resolve-context parity, active registry non-mutation, bounded discovery, and skill guidance.
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep tests focused on behavior-level verification rather than help text or mock routing alone.
tasks.test_strategy: Run targeted unit/e2e tests during implementation and rely on final-regression for full project coverage.
